spec.summary: Reads one pipe-delimited line containing principal, annual rate, and years; validates each token as an unsigned decimal with digit-count limits; rejects rates over 100; computes simple interest as principal * rate * years / 100 with COMPUTE ROUNDED into PIC 9(7)V99; displays INTEREST= followed by a 10-character zero-padded edited value, or an error message.

inputs.name: principal-amount
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99

inputs.name: annual-rate
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

inputs.name: years-count
inputs.format: token 3, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 99: unsigned number, 2 integer digits, max 99

outputs.name: printed-interest
outputs.format: PIC 9(7).99, exactly 10 characters, zero-padded, real decimal point, e.g. INTEREST=0000100.00

business_rules: The ACCEPT buffer is PIC X(256); the actual line length is variable and is not padded to 256.
The input line must contain exactly two pipe '|' delimiters; otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.
Each token is trimmed and validated character-by-character: only digits 0-9 and at most one '.' are allowed; a sign, letter, space, or second decimal point makes the input invalid.
A decimal point must be followed by at least one digit; a trailing '.' is invalid.
Whole-digit count must be at least 1 and not exceed the field maximum (principal 5, rate 3, years 2); fraction-digit count must not exceed the field maximum (principal 2, rate 2, years 0).
Leading zeros are allowed within the digit-count limits; NUMVAL parses the explicit decimal point exactly.
After validation, NUMVAL converts each raw token; the annual rate must not exceed 100, otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.

Interest is computed exactly as principal-amount * annual-rate * years-count / 100, with intermediate decimals retained; the final result is rounded half away from zero into PIC 9(7)V99 via COMPUTE ... ROUNDED.
If the computed result exceeds PIC 9(7)V99, ON SIZE ERROR displays ERROR:OVERFLOW and stops.
The interest amount is moved to PIC 9(7).99 and displayed as exactly 10 characters with leading zeros and a real decimal point, prefixed by 'INTEREST='.
quirks: Validation rejects '-' before NUMVAL is ever called, so negative input is never reinterpreted as positive.
Years-count validation allows max-fraction = 0, so any decimal point in the years token is invalid.
Whole-digit counting increments for digits before the first decimal point only; digits after a decimal point count as fraction digits.
A token such as '.50' has whole-digits = 0 and is invalid because whole-digits must be at least 1.
COMPUTE ROUNDED rounds the final result to 2 implied decimals; truncation does not occur at each arithmetic operator.
The edited output PIC 9(7).99 always shows leading zeros; no zero suppression is applied.

spec.summary: A COBOL program that reads three pipe-delimited tokens (quantity, unit price, discount percent), validates them character-by-character, computes an exact total with truncation at receiving fields, and displays the invoice total or an error message.

inputs.name: quantity-count
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3): unsigned number, 3 integer digits, max 999

inputs.name: unit-price
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99

inputs.name: discount-percent
inputs.format: token 3, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

outputs.name: printed-total
outputs.format: PIC 9(5).99, 8 characters wide, zero-filled integer part, 2 decimals shown

business_rules: The input line must contain exactly 2 pipe delimiters; otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.

Each token is validated character-by-character: only digits and at most one decimal point are allowed; empty whole part, whole digits exceeding max-whole, fraction digits exceeding max-fraction, or a decimal point followed by zero fraction digits set valid-input to 0.
max-whole is 3 for quantity, 5 for unit price, and 3 for discount percent; max-fraction is 0 for quantity and 2 for unit price and discount percent.
Discount percent must not exceed 100; if it does, ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.

The exact total is computed as quantity-count * unit-price * (100 - discount-percent) / 100; intermediate decimals are exact and truncation occurs only at the receiving field EXACT-TOTAL (PIC 9(8)V9(6), 6 implied decimals).
If exact-total is greater than or equal to 100000, ERROR:OVERFLOW is displayed and the program stops.
EXACT-TOTAL is moved to INVOICE-TOTAL (PIC 9(5)V99) without rounding; digits beyond 2 decimal places are truncated.
INVOICE-TOTAL is moved to PRINTED-TOTAL (PIC 9(5).99); the edited PIC displays exactly 8 characters with leading zeros and an explicit decimal point.
The display statement outputs 'TOTAL=' concatenated with the printed-total field.
edge_cases: Input '1|12.35|0.01' produces output 'TOTAL=00012.34' because 1*12.35*(100-0.01)/100 = 12.348765, truncated to 12.348765 in EXACT-TOTAL, then truncated to 12.34 in INVOICE-TOTAL.
Input '2|50000.00|0.00' produces output 'ERROR:OVERFLOW' because exact-total is 100000.000000, which is >= 100000.
Input '-1|19.99|10.00' produces output 'ERROR:INVALID_INPUT' because the minus sign fails character validation.
Input '1|-19.99|10.00' produces output 'ERROR:INVALID_INPUT' because the minus sign fails character validation.
Input '1|19.99|-1.00' produces output 'ERROR:INVALID_INPUT' because the minus sign fails character validation.
Input '1|19.99|100.01' produces output 'ERROR:INVALID_INPUT' because discount-percent exceeds 100.
quirks: Leading zeros are allowed within the source's digit-count limits; PIC 9 output is zero-filled and only Z suppresses zeros.
No ON SIZE ERROR: results exceeding the receiving PIC width silently lose high-order digits.
EXACT-TOTAL is unsigned: a negative intermediate result is stored without its sign.
Validation rejects signs before NUMVAL is reached; negative input is not reinterpreted as positive.
The ACCEPT text buffer capacity is 256 characters, not a required line length; input is not padded to it.
Literal decimal points are typed in the input tokens; they are not stored in V99 implied-decimal fields.

[static check, line 62] EXACT-TOTAL (PIC 9(8)V9(6): unsigned number, 8 integer digits + 6 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999999.999999) is stored WITHOUT ROUNDED: digits beyond 6 decimal place(s) are TRUNCATED, not rounded (e.g. 12.3333339 is stored as 12.333333, not 12.333334).

[static check, line 70] INVOICE-TOTAL (PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99) is stored WITHOUT ROUNDED: digits beyond 2 decimal place(s) are TRUNCATED, not rounded (e.g. 12.339 is stored as 12.33, not 12.34).

spec.summary: A payroll calculator that reads hours worked and hourly rate from a pipe-delimited input, computes gross pay with overtime, applies progressive tax, and prints formatted totals. Invalid inputs or overflow conditions produce error messages and terminate the program.

inputs.name: hours-worked
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

inputs.name: hourly-rate
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

outputs.name: GROSS
outputs.format: PRINTED-GROSS, PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with explicit decimal point

outputs.name: TAX
outputs.format: PRINTED-TAX, PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with explicit decimal point

outputs.name: NET
outputs.format: PRINTED-NET, PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with explicit decimal point

business_rules: 1. Input line must contain exactly one '|' delimiter; otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is printed and the program stops.

2. Both tokens are validated by validate-number: only digits and a single decimal point are allowed; whole-digits must be between 1 and 3 inclusive; fraction-digits must not exceed 2; a decimal point must be followed by at least one digit.
3. Hours worked and hourly rate are converted from text to numeric using NUMVAL after validation.
4. If hours-worked > 40, gross-pay is computed as 40 * hourly-rate + (hours-worked - 40) * hourly-rate * 1.5 with ROUNDED, and ON SIZE ERROR triggers ERROR:OVERFLOW and stops.
5. If hours-worked <= 40, gross-pay is computed as hours-worked * hourly-rate with ROUNDED.

6. Tax is computed on the rounded gross-pay using progressive brackets: gross-pay <= 500 => gross-pay * 0.10; gross-pay <= 1000 => 50 + (gross-pay - 500) * 0.20; otherwise => 150 + (gross-pay - 1000) * 0.30. All tax computes use ROUNDED.
7. Net pay is computed as gross-pay - tax-amount without ROUNDED and without ON SIZE ERROR.
8. Output line displays "GROSS=" followed by edited gross-pay, "|TAX=" followed by edited tax-amount, and "|NET=" followed by edited net-pay as a single DISPLAY line.
9. PIC 9(7).99 fields are zero-filled with leading zeros and an explicit decimal point; e.g. 700.00 displays as 0000700.00.
edge_cases: Input "-1.00|20.00" triggers ERROR:INVALID_INPUT because the '-' character fails validation.
Input "40.00|-1.00" triggers ERROR:INVALID_INPUT because the '-' character fails validation.
Input "1000.00|20.00" triggers ERROR:INVALID_INPUT because whole-digits = 4 exceeds the limit of 3.
quirks: COMPUTE ROUNDED rounds half away from zero; without ROUNDED, truncation occurs at the receiving field.
GROSS-PAY, TAX-AMOUNT, and NET-PAY are unsigned PIC 9(7)V99 fields; negative intermediate results store without their sign.
Without ON SIZE ERROR on line 70, a NET-PAY result above 9999999.99 silently loses its high-order digits.
DISPLAY concatenates operands with no separators; the output format "GROSS=" printed-gross "|TAX=" printed-tax "|NET=" printed-net produces exact spacing as shown in reference observations.
NUMVAL accepts the external text including the literal decimal point; validation then checks digit count and position before conversion.
The validate-number paragraph rejects input if whole-digits = 0, whole-digits > 3, fraction-digits > 2, or if a decimal point is present with zero fraction-digits.
